Level: A1 
Time: 80 minutes 
Lesson Objectives 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
Introduce themselves and greet others confidently. 
Use to be (positive & negative) in simple sentences. 
Practice speaking about themselves (name, age, job, country). 
Improve communication skills through games and role-plays. 
Teaching Instruments: 
Flashcards (names, countries, jobs) 
Whiteboard / markers 
Worksheets (gap-fill, matching, role-play dialogues) 
Name cards (for greeting activities) 
Projector (optional) 
Lesson Structure 
1. Warm-up (10 minutes) 
Greeting the class: Hello! How are you? 
Quick discussion: “How do we greet people in English?” 
Short pair practice: Students greet each other.

👉 Game: Ball Toss Greeting – throw a soft ball; student who catches says: 
“My name is … I am … years old.” 
2. Vocabulary Presentation (10 minutes) 
Introduce useful words/phrases: 
Hello / Hi / Good morning 
My name is … / I am … 
I am a student / teacher / doctor 
I am from Uzbekistan 
 
Drill pronunciation. 
 
3. Grammar Presentation (15 minutes) 
To Be – Positive / Negative 
I am Aziz / I am not Ali. 
6

She is a student. / She is not a teacher. 
They are friends. / They are not doctors. 
👉 On the board: tables with am / is / are + negative forms 
4. Controlled Practice (15 minutes) 
Gap-fill exercise: 
1. I ___ a student. 
2. My name ___ Dilshod. 
3. He ___ not a doctor. 
4. They ___ friends. 
Sentence correction: 
1. I are a teacher. → I am a teacher. 
2. She am not a nurse. → She is not a nurs 
 
5. Communicative Practice (15 minutes) 
👉 Role-play: Students in pairs introduce themselves. 
A: “Hello! My name is Ali. I am a student.” 
B: “Hi Ali! I am Nodira. I am not a student, I am a teacher.” 
 
Students ask: “Are you …?” → Yes, I am. / No, I’m not. 
6. Reading & Speaking (10 minutes) 
Short text: 
“Hello! My name is Kamola. I am 18 years old. I am a student. I am not a teacher. I am from 
Namangan.” 
Questions: 
1. What is her name? 
2. How old is she? 
3. Is she a teacher? 
4. Where is she from? 
7. Wrap-up (5 minutes) 
Recap greetings, My name is… and to be (negative). 
Students share one new thing they learned. 
Teaching Methods 
Communicative approach 
Role-play and pair work 
Repetition & drilling 
Task-based learning 
Interactive games 
Types of Teaching Activities 
Vocabulary practice 
Grammar drilling 
Pair dialogues 
Reading comprehension 
Role-play & interactive games 
Assessment 
Observation during role-plays and games. 
Correct use of to be in exercises.

Participation in “Find Someone Who…” game. 
Quick oral check: each student introduces themselves using positive + negative. 
Homework (Vazifa) 
1. Write 5 sentences about yourself (use to be positive). 
Example: My name is Diyor. I am 19. I am a student. 
2. Write 3 sentences in negative form about yourself. 
Example: I am not a doctor. I am not 25. 
3. Prepare a short self-introduction (3–4 sentences) to present in the next lesson.

Level: A1 (Beginner) 
Duration: 80 minutes 
Lesson Objectives 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
Introduce and describe their address using simple sentences. 
Recall and pronounce the English alphabet correctly. 
Form and answer Yes/No and Wh-questions with to be. 
Improve speaking, reading, and writing skills through interactive tasks. 
Teaching Instruments 
Whiteboard/Markers 
Flashcards with letters & words 
Printed handouts/worksheets 
Projector (if available) 
Real-life props (map, envelope, example address card) 
Lesson Structure 
1. Warm-up (10 min) 
Greeting & short Q/A: How are you? What day is it today? 
Quick game: Alphabet Race – students stand and say alphabet one by one (A–Z). If someone 
makes a mistake, the group helps.

2. Presentation (15 min) 
Introduce address vocabulary: street, city, country, house number, apartment. (Flashcards/real 
examples). 
 
Teacher models: 
My address is 25 Navoi Street, Andijan, Uzbekistan. 
Students repeat. 
Introduce to be (questions): 
Are you from Andijan? – Yes, I am. / No, I am not. 
Is she your teacher? 
Where are you from? 
 
8

3. Practice (Controlled) (15 min) 
Pair work (Interview): Students ask each other: 
What is your address? 
Where are you from? 
Is your house big? 
 
Worksheet: Fill the blanks with am/is/are in questions. Example: 
1. ___ you from Tashkent? 
2. Where ___ your school? 
3. What ___ your house number? 
 
4. Production (Speaking & Writing) (20 min) 
Speaking Game – Find Someone Who… 
Students walk around asking: Are you from Andijan? Is your street long? etc. 
They tick boxes when they find a match. 
Writing Task: 
Students write 4–5 sentences about their address. Example: 
My name is Ali. I am from Andijan. My address is 15 Amir Temur Street. My house is small. It 
is near a park. 
 
5. Reading Activity (10 min) 
Short passage: 
> Hello! My name is Maria. I am from Spain. My address is 20 Green Street, Madrid. My house 
is big and beautiful. Is your house big? Where are you from? 
Students read aloud, underline to be questions, then answer. 
 
 
7. Assessment / Feedback (3–5 min) 
Oral Q/A with students. 
Quick check of written sentences. 
Praise correct answers, give feedback. 
 
Teaching Methods 
Communicative approach 
Pair & group work 
TPR (Total Physical Response) for alphabet game 
Guided discovery (students form rules from examples) 
 
Types of Learning Activities 
Speaking (dialogues, games) 
Reading (short text) 
Writing (personal sentences)

Listening (teacher modeling & peers) 
 
Assessment 
Participation in games and pair work 
Accuracy in question formation 
Correct use of to be in writing task 
 
Homework (Task) 
1. Write 5 sentences about your address using to be. 
2. Prepare 3 to be questions about your classmates (to ask in the next lesson).

Level: A1 (Beginner) 
Duration: 80 minutes 
Lesson Objectives 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
Recognize and use vocabulary related to professions. 
Form and use Present Simple positive sentences correctly. 
Introduce themselves and others with jobs and daily routines. 
Develop speaking, reading, writing, and listening skills through communicative activities. 
Teaching Instruments 
Whiteboard and markers 
Flashcards with pictures of professions 
Worksheets/handouts 
Short text for reading activity 
Ball or soft toy for game 
Projector (optional) 
Lesson Structure 
1. Warm-up (10 min) 
Greeting & small talk. 
Quick brainstorming: Teacher asks, “What jobs do you know?” and writes answers on board.

Game – Charades: Teacher/one student acts a profession (doctor, teacher, driver), others guess. 
 
2. Presentation (15 min) 
Teach professions vocabulary with flashcards: teacher, doctor, nurse, driver, student, cook, engineer, 
farmer, police officer, etc. 
 
Introduce Present Simple (positive): 
I am a teacher. 
She is a nurse. 
He works in a hospital. 
Rule: Subject + base verb (+s/es for he/she/it). 
 
Write examples on board. Students repeat. 
 
3. Controlled Practice (15 min) 
Worksheet 1 (Fill in the blanks): 
10

1. I ___ (be) a student. 
2. My father ___ (work) in a bank. 
3. She ___ (be) a nurse. 
4. They ___ (work) on a farm. 
 
Pair practice: Students practice short dialogues: 
A: What do you do? 
B: I am a driver. I work in a company 
 
4. Production (Speaking & Writing) (20 min) 
Speaking Game – “Find Someone Who” 
Students ask each other: Do you work? Do you study? Are you a student? 
They tick the sheet when they find a person with that profession. 
 
Writing Task: 
Students write 4–5 sentences about themselves or a family member. Example: 
My name is Ali. I am a student. My father is a doctor. He works in a hospital. My mother is a teacher. 
 
5. Reading Activity (10 min) 
Short passage: 
> Hello! My name is Sara. I am a nurse. I work in a hospital. My brother is a driver. He drives a bus. My 
parents are teachers. They work in a school. 
Students read aloud, underline Present Simple verbs, then answer questions: 
1. What is Sara’s job? 
2. Where does she work? 
3. What is her brother’s job? 
4. Where do her parents work? 
 
6. Games (5–7 min) 
Ball Game: Teacher throws a ball and says a subject (e.g., He). Student must make a Present Simple 
positive sentence (He is a farmer. He works on a farm.). Then throws to another student. 
Memory Game (optional): Place profession flashcards face down. Students flip 2 and make a sentence 
(She is a doctor).

7. Assessment / Feedback (5 min) 
Teacher checks students’ sentences and participation. 
Oral feedback on speaking activity. 
Corrects common errors (verb endings, use of is/are). 
 
Teaching Methods 
Communicative approach 
Pair and group work 
Visual aids (flashcards, pictures) 
Repetition & drilling 
Games for engagement 
 
Types of Learning Activities 
Speaking (role-plays, dialogues, interviews) 
Reading (short text comprehension) 
Writing (personal sentences) 
Listening (to teacher and peers) 
 
Assessment 
Class participation 
Accuracy in Present Simple usage 
Reading comprehension answers 
Writing task evaluation 
Homework (Task) 
1. Write 6–7 sentences about the professions in your family. 
2. Find 3 pictures of different jobs (from magazine/phone) and write sentences: 
This is a doctor. He works in a hospital.

Teaching Instruments 
Whiteboard and markers 
Flashcards with job pictures 
Worksheets/handouts 
A ball or soft toy (for games)

Lesson Structure 
1. Warm-up (10 minutes) 
Greeting & quick review: Teacher asks: “What jobs do you know?” (students brainstorm). 
Game – Mime the Job: One student acts out a profession (doctor, teacher, driver). Class guesses.

2. Presentation (15 minutes) 
Teach/review job vocabulary with flashcards (doctor, teacher, driver, nurse, farmer, cook, student, 
engineer, police officer). 
 
Introduce Present Simple negative: 
I don’t work in a hospital. 
She doesn’t work in an office. 
 
Write rules on board: 
I/You/We/They + don’t + verb 
He/She/It + doesn’t + verb 
 
3. Controlled Practice (15 minutes) 
12

Worksheet 1 (Fill in the blanks): 
1. A driver __ work in a hospital. 
2. My father __ work in a shop. 
3. Teachers __ work in banks. 
4. He __ work in a school, he works in a hotel. 
5. They __ work on a farm. 
Sentence Transformation: Change into negative. 
1. She works in a hospital. → ______ 
2. They work in a shop. → ______ 
 
4. Speaking Practice (15 minutes) 
Pair Work – True or False: 
Student A says a sentence: “A nurse works in a bank.” 
Student B corrects: “No, a nurse doesn’t work in a bank. A nurse works in a hospital.” 
Find Someone Who Game: 
Example questions: 
Do you work in a hospital? 
Do you want to be a pilot? 
Students walk around, ask, and record classmates’ names. 
5. Reading Activity (10 minutes) 
Short text: 
> “My name is Tom. I am a driver. I don’t work in a hospital. I drive a bus. My wife is a teacher. She 
doesn’t work in a bank. She works in a school.” 
Questions: 
1. What is Tom’s job? 
2. Where does he work? 
3. Does he work in a hospital? 
4. What is his wife’s job? 
5. Does she work in a bank? 
6. Games (7–8 minutes) 
Ball Game: Teacher throws a ball and gives a subject + job. Student makes a negative sentence. 
Teacher: He / doctor 
Student: He doesn’t work in a hospital. He is a driver. 
Flashcard Race: Teacher shows two jobs. Students must quickly say one positive and one negative 
sentence. 
7. Assessment / Feedback (5 minutes)

Teacher checks students’ answers from worksheets. 
Oral correction of common mistakes (don’t/doesn’t + base verb). 
Praise active participation.

Level: A1 (Beginner)

Lesson Objectives 
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to: 
Recognize, say, and use numbers 1–100 in English. 
Form and use Present Simple questions (Do/Does…?) correctly. 
Ask and answer simple questions using numbers (e.g., Do you have two brothers?). 
Improve speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills through engaging activities. 
Teaching Instruments 
Whiteboard & markers 
Number flashcards (1–100) 
Worksheets/handouts 
Dice or number cards (for games) 
Ball or soft toy (for Q&A game) 
Projector (optional) 
Lesson Structure 
1. Warm-up (10 minutes) 
Greeting. Quick review of basic numbers (1–20).

Game – Counting Chain: Each student says one number in order (1, 2, 3…). If a student makes a mistake, class 
helps correct. 
Teacher asks: “Do you know big numbers?” and writes 10, 20, 50, 100. 
2. Presentation (15 minutes) 
Teach/review numbers 1–100 with flashcards or board. 
Introduce Present Simple Questions (Yes/No): 
Do you have two sisters? – Yes, I do. / No, I don’t. 
Does he have three brothers? – Yes, he does. / No, he doesn’t. 
Highlight structure on board: 
Do/Does + subject + base verb + object? 
3. Controlled Practice (15 minutes) 
Worksheet Exercises: 
1. Complete the questions: 
___ you have two pens? 
___ your father work in a bank? 
___ they play football? 
___ she have one brother? 
2. Answer with Yes/No. 
14

Pair work: Students ask each other: 
Do you have three cousins? 
Does your mother work in a hospital? 
 
4. Speaking Practice (15 minutes) 
Game – Find Someone Who… 
Find a classmate who has: 
2 brothers 
1 sister 
3 books in their bag 
10 pens 
Students ask: “Do you have…?” and write names. 
Ball Game: Teacher throws ball and asks: “Do you have 5 pencils?” Student answers and asks another question to 
next student. 
5. Reading Activity (10 minutes) 
Short text: 
> “My name is Ali. I have two brothers and one sister. My father works in a shop. My mother has three books. We 
all play football together.” 
Questions: 
1. Does Ali have two brothers? 
2. Does he have one sister? 
3. Does his father work in a hospital? 
4. Does his mother have three books? 
6. Writing Task (7 minutes) 
Students write 5 questions and answers using numbers. 
Example: 
Do you have two sisters? – No, I don’t. I have one sister. 
Does your father work in an office? – Yes, he does. 
7. Games (5–7 minutes) 
Dice Game: Roll dice (or number cards). Students must make a question with the number. 
Example: Roll 4 → Do you have four pens? 
Number Bingo: Teacher calls out numbers, students cross them off on bingo cards. 
8. Assessment / Feedback (5 minutes) 
Check worksheet answers. 
Observe speaking activities. 
Give feedback on common errors (Do/Does usage).

Game-based activities

Writing practice 
Games (Bingo, Dice, Ball)

Correct answers in reading comprehension 
Written task quality 
 
Homework (Task) 
1. Write 10 Present Simple questions using numbers. Example: 
Do you have three friends? 
Does your father have two cars? 
2. Ask your family members 5 of your questions and write their answers.

Lesson Objectives 
Students will recall and correctly use the days of the week. 
Students will understand how to form Present Continuous questions and negatives. 
Students will practice asking and answering about current actions using Present Continuous.

Teaching Instruments 
Whiteboard, markers 
Flashcards with days of the week 
Worksheets (fill-in-the-blanks, matching, sentence building) 
Pictures or short videos of people doing actions 
Realia (classroom objects, timetable chart)

1. Warm-up (5 minutes) 
Greeting.

Quick chant: students say days of the week together. Teacher points randomly; students say the 
word. 
 
2. Presentation (15 minutes) 
Vocabulary: Days of the week 
Introduce on the board, practice pronunciation. 
Use rhythm/song (optional). 
 
Grammar focus: 
Question: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb+ing? (e.g., Is he studying?) 
Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + verb+ing (e.g., They are not working.) 
Compare positive, question, negative on the board with examples. 
 
3. Practice (20 minutes) 
18

Vocabulary practice: 
Matching game: flashcards in the wrong order → students arrange correctly. 
“What day is today?” questions. 
 
Grammar practice: 
Sentence transformation: turn positives into negatives. 
Make questions from prompts: (you / study English now? → Are you studying English now?) 
Pair activity: students ask and answer using Present Continuous questions. 
 
4. Production (25 minutes) 
Game 1: “Class Survey” 
Students walk around asking: Are you writing now? Are you reading? They tick answers on a 
worksheet. 
 
Game 2: “Day Detective” 
Teacher says: Today is Tuesday. Are we studying English? → Students answer using Present 
Continuous negative: No, we are not studying math. We are studying English. 
 
Role-play: 
Students act out actions; classmates ask questions (Is he dancing?). Student answers 
negatively/positively. 
 
5. Cool-down (5 minutes) 
Days of the week circle: students say them in order one by one. 
Reflection: each student makes one question and one negative sentence using Present 
Continuous.

Group (games, surveys, role-play)

Teacher monitors pair/group tasks.

Oral check: students form Present Continuous questions and negatives. 
Quick worksheet: 5 sentences to rewrite as questions/negatives.

Write the days of the week in order + one sentence for each day. 
Write 5 Present Continuous questions and 5 negatives about your family or friends.

Lesson Objectives 
Students will review all main vocabulary and grammar learned in previous units. 
Students will practice exam-style tasks in speaking, writing, listening, and reading. 
Students will gain confidence and strategies for upcoming tests. 
Students will demonstrate knowledge through interactive games and mini-tests. 
 
Teaching Aids 
Flashcards (vocabulary review: clothes, food, seasons, daily routine, travel, city life, jobs, 
holidays, transport, etc.).

Audio clips for listening.

Projector (optional for games).

1. Warm-up (10 minutes)

Lesson Structure (80 minutes) 
 
1. Warm-up (10 minutes) 
 • Teacher asks quick questions: 
 • Can you swim?

• Could you ride a bike when you were five? 
 • May I come in? 
 • What might happen tomorrow?

 • Teacher explains uses with examples: 
 • Can → ability / permission (I can play football. Can I open the window?)
